questions.question: Let $f\left(x\right) = \frac{x}{{\left(1 + {x}^{n}\right)}^{\frac{1}{n}}},x \in ℝ - \left( - 1\right),n \in ℕ,n > 2$. If ${f}^{n}\left(x\right) = (fofof....$ upto $n$ times) $\left(x\right)$, then $\underset{n \to \infty }{\lim }{ \int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{n - 2}\left({f}^{n}\left(x\right)\right)dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \frac{x}{{\left(1 + {x}^{n}\right)}^{\frac{1}{n}}},x \in ℝ - \left( - 1\right),n \in ℕ,n > 2$,

${f}^{n}\left(x\right) = (fofof....$ upto $n$ times) $\left(x\right)$,

Now finding $f\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = \frac{f\left(x\right)}{{\left(1 + {\left(f\left(x\right)\right)}^{n}\right)}^{\frac{1}{n}}} \implies f\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = \frac{\frac{x}{{\left(1 + {x}^{n}\right)}^{\frac{1}{n}}}}{{\left(1 + {\left(\frac{x}{{\left(1 + {x}^{n}\right)}^{\frac{1}{n}}}\right)}^{n}\right)}^{\frac{1}{n}}} \implies f\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = \frac{x}{{\left(1 + 2{x}^{n}\right)}^{\frac{1}{n}}}$

Similarly, ${f}^{n}\left(x\right) = \frac{x}{{\left(1 + n{x}^{n}\right)}^{\frac{1}{n}}}$

Now solving the integral we get,

$I = { \int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{x}^{n - 1}}{{\left(1 + n{x}^{n}\right)}^{\frac{1}{n}}}dx$

Now let, $1 + n{x}^{n} = {t}^{n} \implies {n}^{2}{x}^{n - 1}dx = n{t}^{n - 1}dt I = { \int }_{1}^{{\left(1 + n\right)}^{\frac{1}{n}}}\frac{\frac{1}{n}{t}^{n - 1}dt}{t} \implies I = {\left(\frac{1}{n}\frac{{t}^{n - 1}}{n - 1}\right)}_{1}^{{\left(1 + n\right)}^{\frac{1}{n}}} \implies I = \frac{1}{n\left(n - 1\right)}\left({\left(1 + n\right)}^{1 - \frac{1}{n}} - 1\right)$

Now solving the limit we get,

$\underset{n \to \infty }{\lim }\frac{{\left(1 + n\right)}^{1 - \frac{1}{n}} - 1}{n\left(n - 1\right)}$

Now let $n = \frac{1}{h}$ so the limit changes to,

$\underset{h \to 0}{\lim }\frac{{\left(1 + \frac{1}{h}\right)}^{1 - h} - 1}{\frac{1}{h}\left(\frac{1}{h} - 1\right)} = \underset{h \to 0}{\lim }\frac{\left(1 + \frac{1}{h}\left(1 - h\right)\right) - 1}{\frac{1}{h}\left(\frac{1}{h} - 1\right)} = \underset{h \to 0}{\lim }\frac{\left(1 - h\right)}{\left(\frac{1}{h} - 1\right)} = \underset{h \to 0}{\lim }\frac{h\left(1 - h\right)}{\left(1 - h\right)} = \underset{h \to 0}{\lim }h = 0$

questions.question: Let $\underset{0⩽x⩽2}{Max}\left(\frac{9 - {x}^{2}}{5 - x}\right) = \alpha$ and $\underset{0⩽x⩽2}{\mathrm{Min}}\left(\frac{9 - {x}^{2}}{5 - x}\right) = \beta$. If ${ \int }_{\beta - \frac{8}{3}}^{2\alpha - 1}Max\left(\frac{9 - {x}^{2}}{5 - x},x\right)dx = {\alpha }_{1} + {\alpha }_{2}{\log }_{e}\left(\frac{8}{15}\right)$, then ${\alpha }_{1} + {\alpha }_{2}$ is equal to ______
questions.explanation:
Here $y = \frac{9 - {x}^{2}}{5 - x} = 5 + x + \frac{16}{x - 5} \frac{dy}{dx} = 1 - \frac{16}{{\left(x - 5\right)}^{2}}$

When $\frac{dy}{dx} = 0 \implies 1 - \frac{16}{{\left(x - 5\right)}^{2}} = 0$

So critical point is $x = 1$ in $\left(0,2\right)$

Now we get $y\left(0\right) = \frac{9}{5},y\left(1\right) = 2,y\left(2\right) = \frac{5}{3}$

So $\alpha = 2$ and $\beta = \frac{5}{3} I = { \int }_{ - 1}^{3}\max \left(\frac{9 - {x}^{2}}{5 - x},x\right) I = { \int }_{ - 1}^{\frac{9}{5}}\left(5 + x + \frac{16}{x - 5}\right)dx + { \int }_{\frac{9}{5}}^{3}xdx = {\left(5x + \frac{{x}^{2}}{2} + 16\ln \left(x - 5\right)\right)}_{ - 1}^{\frac{9}{5}} + {\left(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right)}_{\frac{9}{5}}^{3} I = 18 + 16\ln \left(\frac{8}{15}\right) {\alpha }_{1} = 18$ and ${\alpha }_{2} = 16 \implies {\alpha }_{1} + {\alpha }_{2} = 34$

questions.question: Let ${f}_{n} = { \int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}\left({ \sum }_{k = 1}^{n}{\sin }^{k - 1}x\right)\left({ \sum }_{k = 1}^{n}(2k - 1){\sin }^{k - 1}x\right)\cos xdx,n \in ℕ.$ Then ${f}_{21} - {f}_{20}$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
Given,

${f}_{n} = { \int }_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left({ \sum }_{k = 1}^{n}{\sin }^{k - 1}x\right)\left({ \sum }_{k = 1}^{n}(2k - 1){\sin }^{k - 1}x\right)\cos xdx$

Now let, $\sin x = t \implies \cos xdx = dt$

So, ${f}_{n} = { \int }_{0}^{1}\left({ \sum }_{k = 1}^{n}(t{)}^{k - 1}\right)\left({ \sum }_{k = 1}^{n}(2k - 1)(t{)}^{k - 1}\right)dt \implies {f}_{n} = { \int }_{0}^{1}\left(1 + t + {t}^{2}.... + {t}^{n - 1}\right)\left(1 + 3t + 5{t}^{2} + ..... + \left(2n - 1\right){t}^{n - 1}\right)dt$

Now multiply and divide by $\sqrt{t}$ we get,

$\implies {f}_{n} = { \int }_{0}^{1}\frac{\left({t}^{\frac{1}{2}} + {t}^{\frac{3}{2}} + {t}^{\frac{5}{2}}.... + {t}^{\frac{2n - 1}{2}}\right)}{\sqrt{t}}\left(1 + 3t + 5{t}^{2} + ..... + \left(2n - 1\right){t}^{n - 1}\right)dt \implies {f}_{n} = { \int }_{0}^{1}\left({t}^{\frac{1}{2}} + {t}^{\frac{3}{2}} + {t}^{\frac{5}{2}}.... + {t}^{\frac{2n - 1}{2}}\right)\left({t}^{\frac{ - 1}{2}} + 3{t}^{\frac{1}{2}} + 5{t}^{\frac{3}{2}} + ..... + \left(2n - 1\right){t}^{\frac{2n - 3}{2}}\right)dt$

Now let ${t}^{\frac{1}{2}} + {t}^{\frac{3}{2}} + {t}^{\frac{5}{2}}.... + {t}^{\frac{2n - 1}{2}} = z \implies \frac{1}{2}\left({t}^{\frac{ - 1}{2}} + 3{t}^{\frac{1}{2}} + 5{t}^{\frac{3}{2}} + ..... + \left(2n - 1\right){t}^{\frac{2n - 3}{2}}\right)dt = dz$

Hence, the integral becomes,

$\implies {f}_{n} = 2{ \int }_{0}^{n}zdz \implies {f}_{n} = {\left({z}^{2}\right)}_{0}^{n} = {n}^{2}$

Hence, ${f}_{21} - {f}_{20} = {21}^{2} - {20}^{2} = 41$

questions.question: If $f\left(\theta \right) = \sin \theta + { \int }_{ - \frac{\pi }{2}}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}\left(\sin \theta + t\cos \theta \right) \cdot f\left(t\right)dt$, then $\left({ \int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}f\left(\theta \right)d\theta \right)$ is
questions.explanation:
Given $f\left(\theta \right) = \sin \theta + { \int }_{ - \frac{\pi }{2}}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}\left(\sin \theta + t\cos \theta \right)f\left(t\right)dt f\left(\theta \right) = \sin \theta + \sin \theta { \int }_{ - \frac{\pi }{2}}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}f\left(t\right)dt + \cos \theta { \int }_{ - \frac{\pi }{2}}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}tf\left(t\right)dt$

Let $A = { \int }_{ - \frac{\pi }{2}}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}f\left(t\right)dt,B = { \int }_{ - \frac{\pi }{2}}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}tf\left(t\right)dt$

So $f\left(\theta \right) = \sin \theta + A\sin \theta + B\cos \theta$

i.e. $f\left(\theta \right) = \left(A + 1\right)\sin \theta + B\cos \theta A = { \int }_{ - \frac{\pi }{2}}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}\left(\left(A + 1\right)\sin t + B\cos t\right)dt \implies A = \left(A + 1\right){ \int }_{ - \frac{\pi }{2}}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}\sin tdt + B{ \int }_{ - \frac{\pi }{2}}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}\cos tdt \implies A = 2B \dots \left(1\right) B = { \int }_{ - \frac{\pi }{2}}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}t\left(\left(A + 1\right)\sin t + B\cos t\right)dt \implies B = { \int }_{ - \frac{\pi }{2}}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}t\left(A + 1\right)\sin tdt \implies B = \left(A + 1\right)2{ \int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}t\sin tdt \implies B = \left(A + 1\right)2 \implies 2A + 2 - B = 0⋯\left(2\right)$

After solving

$B = - \frac{2}{3},A = - \frac{4}{3} \left({ \int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}f\left(\theta \right)d\theta \right) = \left({ \int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}\left( - \frac{1}{3}\sin \theta - \frac{2}{3}\cos \theta \right)d\theta \right) = \left( - \frac{1}{3}{ \int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}\sin \theta d\theta - \frac{2}{3}{ \int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}\cos \theta d\theta \right) = 1$

questions.question: Let $[t]$ denote the largest integer less than or equal to $t$. If $\int_0^3\left(\left[x^2\right]+\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right]\right) \mathrm{d} x=\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b} \sqrt{2}-\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{5}+\mathrm{c} \sqrt{6}-\sqrt{7}$, where $\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c} \in \mathbf{Z}$, then $\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}+\mathrm{c}$ is equal to_______
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & \int_0^3\left[x^2\right] d x+\int_0^3\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right] d x \\ & =\int_0^1 0 d x+\int_1^{12} 1 d x+\int_{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}} 2 d x\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & +\int_{\sqrt{3}}^2 3 \mathrm{dx}+\int_2^{\sqrt{5}} 4 \mathrm{dx}+\int_{\sqrt{5}}^{\sqrt{6}} 5 \mathrm{dx} \\ & +\int_{\sqrt{6}}^{\sqrt{7}} 6 \mathrm{dx}+\int_{\sqrt{7}}^{\sqrt{8}} 7 \mathrm{dx}+\int_{\sqrt{8}}^3 8 \mathrm{dx} \\ & +\int_0^{\sqrt{2}} 0 \mathrm{dx}+\int_{\sqrt{2}}^2 1 \mathrm{dx} \\ & +\int_2^{\sqrt{6}} 2 \mathrm{dx}+\int_{\sqrt{6}}^{\sqrt{8}} 3 \mathrm{dx}+\int_{\sqrt{8}}^3 4 \mathrm{dx}=31-6 \sqrt{2}-\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{5} \\ & -2 \sqrt{6}-\sqrt{7} \\ & \mathrm{a}=31 \quad \mathrm{~b}=-6 \quad \mathrm{c}=-2 \\ & \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}+\mathrm{c}=31-6-2=23\end{aligned}$

questions.question: Let for $x \in ℝ,{S}_{0}\left(x\right) = x,{S}_{k}\left(x\right) = {C}_{k}x + k{ \int }_{0}^{x}{S}_{k - 1}\left(t\right)dt$ where ${C}_{0} = 1,{C}_{k} = 1 - { \int }_{0}^{1}{S}_{k - 1}\left(x\right)dx,k = 1,2,3, \dots$ Then ${S}_{2}\left(3\right) + 6{C}_{3}$ is equal to $_______.$
questions.explanation:
Given,

${S}_{0}\left(x\right) = x,{S}_{k}\left(x\right) = {C}_{k}x + k{ \int }_{0}^{x}{S}_{k - 1}\left(t\right)dt$

Now for ${S}_{0}\left(x\right) = x,{C}_{0} = 1$

Now solving, ${C}_{k} = 1 - { \int }_{0}^{1}{S}_{k - 1}\left(x\right)dx$ for $k = 1$ we get,

${C}_{1} = 1 - { \int }_{0}^{1}xdx = \frac{1}{2}$

Now putting $k = 1$ in ${S}_{k}\left(x\right) = {C}_{k}x + k{ \int }_{0}^{x}{S}_{k - 1}\left(t\right)dt$ we get,

$\implies {S}_{1}\left(x\right) = \frac{x}{2} + 1 \cdot { \int }_{0}^{x}tdt = \frac{x}{2} + \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}$

Now for $k = 2$ we get,

${C}_{2} = 1 - { \int }_{0}^{1}\left(\frac{x}{2} + \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right)dx = \frac{7}{12}$

And ${S}_{2}\left(x\right) = \frac{7}{12}x + 2{ \int }_{0}^{x}\left(\frac{t}{2} + \frac{{t}^{2}}{2}\right)dt \implies {S}_{2}\left(x\right) = \frac{7x}{12} + \frac{{x}^{2}}{2} + \frac{{x}^{3}}{3}$

Now taking $k = 3$ we get,

${C}_{3} = 1 - { \int }_{0}^{1}\left(\frac{7x}{12} + \frac{{x}^{2}}{2} + \frac{{x}^{3}}{3}\right)dx = \frac{11}{24}$

Now finding the value of${S}_{2}\left(3\right) + 6 \cdot {C}_{3}$ we get,

${S}_{2}\left(3\right) + 6 \cdot {C}_{3} = \frac{7 \times 3}{12} + \frac{{3}^{2}}{2} + \frac{{3}^{3}}{3} + 6 \times \frac{11}{24} \implies {S}_{2}\left(3\right) + 6 \cdot {C}_{3} = \frac{61}{4} + \frac{11}{4} = 18$

questions.question: Let ${a}_{n} = { \int }_{ - 1}^{n}\left(1 + \frac{x}{2} + \frac{{x}^{2}}{3} + \dots + \frac{{x}^{n - 1}}{n}\right)dx$ for every $n \in N$. Then the sum of all the elements of the set $\left(n \in N : {a}_{n} \in \left(2,30\right)\right)$ is _________.

If the integral $525{ \int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}\sin 2x{\cos }^{\frac{11}{2}}x{\left(1 + {\cos }^{\frac{5}{2}}x\right)}^{\frac{1}{2}}dx$ is equal to $\left(n\sqrt{2}−64\right)$, then $n$ is equal to ________
questions.explanation:
Let,

$I = { \int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi }{2}}\sin 2x{\cos }^{\frac{11}{2}}x{\left(1 + {\cos }^{\frac{5}{2}}x\right)}^{\frac{1}{2}}dx$

Let $\cos x = {t}^{2} \implies \sin xdx = - 2tdt ∴I = - 4{ \int }_{1}^{0}{t}^{2}⋅{t}^{11}\sqrt{\left(1 + {t}^{5}\right)}\left(t\right)dt \implies I = 4{ \int }_{0}^{1}{t}^{14}\sqrt{\left(1 + {t}^{5}\right)}dt$

Now, let $1 + {t}^{5} = {k}^{2} \implies 5{t}^{4}dt = 2kdk ∴I = 4⋅{ \int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}{\left({k}^{2}−1\right)}^{2}⋅k \cdot \frac{2k}{5}dk \implies I = \frac{8}{5}{ \int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}{k}^{6}−2{k}^{4} + {k}^{2}dk \implies I = \frac{8}{5}{\left(\frac{{k}^{7}}{7}−\frac{2{k}^{5}}{5} + \frac{{k}^{3}}{3}\right)}_{1}^{\sqrt{2}} \implies I = \frac{8}{5}\left(\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{7}−\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{5} + \frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}−\frac{1}{7} + \frac{2}{5}−\frac{1}{3}\right) \implies I = \frac{8}{5}\left(\frac{22\sqrt{2}}{105}−\frac{8}{105}\right) \implies 525⋅I = 176\sqrt{2}−64$

Hence, on comparing we get, $n = 176$

questions.question: Let $r_k=\frac{\int_0^1\left(1-x^7\right)^k d x}{\int_0^1\left(1-x^7\right)^{k+1} d x}, k \in \mathbb{N}$. Then the value of $\sum_{k=1}^{10} \frac{1}{7\left(r_k-1\right)}$ is equal to________
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & I_K=\int 1 \cdot\left(1-x^7\right)^K d x \\ & I_K=\left.\left(1-x^7\right)^K x\right|_0 ^1+7 K \int_0^1\left(1-x^7\right)^{K-1} x^6 \cdot x d x \\ & I_K=-7 K \int_0^1\left(1-x^7\right)^{K-1}\left(\left(1-x^7\right)-1\right) d x \\ & I_K=-7 K I_K+7 K I_{K-1} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{I_K}{I_{K+1}}=\frac{7 K+8}{7 K+7}\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & r_K=\frac{7 K+8}{7 \mathrm{~K}+7} \\ & \mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{K}}-1=\frac{1}{7(\mathrm{~K}+1)} \\ & \Rightarrow 7\left(\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{K}}-1\right)=\frac{1}{\mathrm{~K}+1} \\ & \sum_{\mathrm{K}=1}^{10}(\mathrm{~K}+1)=11(6)-1=65\end{aligned}$ .

questions.question: The value of $k \in \mathrm{N}$ for which the integral $I_n=\int_0^1\left(1-x^k\right)^n d x, n \in \mathbb{N}$, satisfies $147 I_{20}=148 I_{21}$ is
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & I_n=\int_0^1\left(1-x^k\right)^n \cdot 1 d x \\ & I_n=\left(1-x^k\right)^n \cdot x-n k \int_0^1\left(1-x^k\right)^{n-1} \cdot x^{k-1} \cdot d x \\ & I_n=n k \int_0^1\left[\left(1-x^k\right)^n-\left(1-x^k\right)^{n-1}\right] d x \\ & I_n=n k I_n-n k I_n \\ & \frac{I_n}{I_{n-1}}=\frac{n k}{n k+1} \\ & \frac{I_{21}}{I_{20}}=\frac{21 k}{1+21 k} \\ & =\frac{147}{148} \Rightarrow k=7\end{aligned}$ !

questions.question: Let ${I}_{n}\left(x\right) = { \int }_{0}^{x}\frac{1}{{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}}dt,n = 1,2,3, \dots .$ Then
questions.explanation:
Given,

${I}_{n}\left(x\right) = { \int }_{0}^{x}\frac{dt}{{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}}$

Applying integration by parts we get,

$\implies {I}_{n}\left(x\right) = {\left(\frac{t}{{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}}\right)}_{0}^{x} - { \int }_{0}^{x}n{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{ - n - 1} \cdot 2{t}^{2} \implies {I}_{n}\left(x\right) = \frac{x}{{\left({x}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}} + 2n{ \int }_{0}^{x}\frac{{t}^{2}}{{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n + 1}}dt \implies {I}_{n}\left(x\right) = \frac{x}{{\left({x}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}} + 2n{ \int }_{0}^{x}\frac{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right) - 5}{{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n + 1}}dt \implies {I}_{n}\left(x\right) = \frac{x}{{\left({x}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}} + 2n{ \int }_{0}^{x}\frac{dt}{{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}} - 10n{ \int }_{0}^{x}\frac{dt}{{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n + 1}} \implies {I}_{n}\left(x\right) = \frac{x}{{\left({x}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}} + 2n{I}_{n}\left(x\right) - 10n{I}_{n + 1}\left(x\right) \implies 10n{I}_{n + 1}\left(x\right) + \left(1 - 2n\right){I}_{n}\left(x\right) = \frac{x}{{\left({x}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}} \implies 10n{I}_{n + 1}\left(x\right) + \left(1 - 2n\right){I}_{n}\left(x\right) = x{{I}^{'}}_{n}$ {where ${{I}^{'}}_{n} = \frac{1}{{\left({x}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}}$ we get by differentiating ${I}_{n}\left(x\right) = { \int }_{0}^{x}\frac{dt}{{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}}$ }

Now put $n = 5$

We get, $50{I}_{6} - 9{I}_{5} = x{I}_{5}^{'}$
